newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on disappointing profits.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on disappointing profits.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell Monday in light trading amid market disenchantment with first quarter earnings reports.

"It's all down to company earnings. There's been all this talk of an economic recovery, but in reports posted so far, we just don't see it yet," one trader said. "Mexican ADRs were hammered, but the Dow was fine."
The leading IPC share index ended down 26.43 points, or 0.70 percent, at 3,756.19. The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile ended up 44.15 points at 6,783.02.
"Earnings have shown little growth in sales, many firms still have financial problems, and that's the big ones. Don't even look at the smaller ones," the desk trader added.

Dealers said a decline in Telmex ADRs, down 7/8 to 40-5/8 in New York trading, weighed most on the Mexican market. The telecomms firm's L shares ended down 14 centavos (2 cents) at 16.30 pesos ($2.04).

Dealers also drew attention to a poor performance by ADRs listed by beverage firm Coca-Cola Femsa, which dropped 2-3/4 to 33-1/2 while its peso shares fell 2.90 pesos (36 cents) to 26.90 pesos ($3.37).
"Coca-Cola Femsa's bottom line earnings were apparently good, but only due to non-cash items," one trader said.
Televisa continued its recent slide on Wall Street, off 1-1/4 to 22-3/4, while the media group's CPO shares fell 1.90 pesos (24 cents) to 92.30 pesos ($11.57) in Mexico.

Some traders attributed Televisa's fall to a persistent adverse reaction to earnings posted last week, while others said the market was uneasy over a battle for boardroom control after the recent death of its long-serving Chairman and President Emilio Azcarraga Milmo.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, slid two centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.75 pesos (34 cents) on profit-taking after gains last week coupled with fears of forthcoming interest rate hikes.
On the broad market, 107 stocks were traded, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 59 to 25.
